chunks: From him, from Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mansur, from Hisham ibn Salim, who said:
I asked him about the nasamah (one-fifth of a slave), so he said: 'Free the one who frees his own self (by paying the ransom).'.

key_terms.أَغْنَى: Enriched or made wealthy; here meaning to pay the price or ransom.
key_terms.النَّسَمَة: One-fifth of a slave; a share of a slave's value used for manumission.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on freeing a slave by paying one's own ransom in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of *mudabbad* (self-purchasing) by instructing the individual to 'free themselves' through payment, emphasizing personal agency in fulfilling the contractual obligation. This ruling underscores the Shia legal principle that the slave retains the right to negotiate and execute their own manumission, distinguishing it from master-initiated freeing. The phrase 'man aghna nafsahu' highlights the financial responsibility placed on the enslaved person to accumulate or secure the agreed-upon value for their liberty.
